A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
bipolar hosts with a higher ET value are more prone to CTC, while those with a lower ET value suffer more from charge flux imbalance.
the mm-hybrid provides a better compromise between CTC formation and charge flux balance, whereas the ppp-hybrid offers a better compromise between the two factors in the case of a blue dopant.
bipolar hosts with high ET values are preferable for PhOLEDs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the propensity for CTC formation in a bipolar host is a more critical factor in PhOLED performance than the balance between charge flux across the EML.
the bipolar hybrid host with the highest ET value is the most suitable for PhOLEDs.
the bipolar host should be chosen to strike a balance between charge flux and charge transfer, the former being the more important factor for the fabrication of PhOLEDs.
